P1.evidence: Three-part frame with a self-positioning addition — 'I'm more of a mentality coach, mindset coach, however you want to call it here, and want to make sure that we see what your goals are, where you're currently at, see if we can help you bridge the [gap]. If not, I'm still here to point you in the right direction.' Agreement taken ('Perfect. Yep. Perfect.'). Open question run, and the rep checked the pronunciation of the prospect's name, which is a good rapport move.

P2.evidence: Age, weight and height taken in one clean question. Training history, results and nutrition covered well, including the eating window. But injuries and health conditions were never asked at all — of a former professional swimmer with a jujitsu and acrobatics background, which is a population with a high base rate of shoulder and joint history. Occupation surfaced only at 00:48:52, after the objection, and only as a rapport move. Sleep and energy absent.

P3.evidence: Ran the 1-10 physique and mobility scales, pushed for the specific target (84 kg lean), and asked the bridge question — 'is there something more personal behind it for just wanting to be stronger?' — which produced the family answer. Followed properly into who else it affects: 'What do you mean by, for your family?' → wife and son. The rep also ran the six-pack contrast argument well and the prospect delivered the intended conclusion himself: 'the main goal is not six-pack... you are a man, you are a father, and you had to be strong for your son.' The reflection at 00:27:24 was clean. Never asked what physical thing he cannot do now.

P4.evidence: Established the on-off pattern going back to 18 — 'I went to the gym for one, two years, then skip it for one, two years, then again' — and the rep named it ('consistency'). But he named it rather than making the prospect name it, which is what P4e asks for. The 'why now and not six months ago' line was pressed twice and produced only 'I don't know what to say more'. The root-cause question was never asked.

P5.evidence: The two-year question was asked properly — 'how do you think that it would look like for you in six months to a year when you just keep doing the exact same thing as you're currently doing and don't make that change?' The prospect defeated it: 'I'll keep going. I am the person who can go far away. If I have a goal. So that's why I will keep trying.' The rep converted that into agreement ('So you wouldn't be able to settle for less') rather than pressing, which is the second time in this batch the consequence frame has failed against a self-reliant prospect and been abandoned rather than reframed. No 'why not', no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: The belief question was asked properly and twice — 'do you feel like you're then actually going to be able to get more functionality, to become more lean, to get stronger, to become a better role model?' → 'Of course. Of course.' A 1-10 was run and returned 9, and the rep correctly probed what was keeping it off 10 (travel and nutrition) and addressed it. But the all-in question was never asked, and P6c was missed outright: the prospect had already said 'the price is also half his own place' at 00:37:10, signalling that cost was a live decision factor, and the rep moved to price without resolving it.

P11.evidence: No agreement was reached; the prospect deferred by 24 hours. Nothing to collect, book, sign or send.

objection_plays.detail: The cleanest OA attempt in the batch and still incomplete. The rep ran the isolation — 'is it really about thinking if it's actually a fit or is it mainly about the money aspect?' → 'No, not about the money' — then 'tell me exactly, how are you going to think about it?' and 'is it like a specific part you want to think about? Or is it like the whole picture?' He also used a strong situational mirror, asking the prospect, a sales manager, what he does when his own customers say they want to think about it. What did not run: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision', and the identity question. He asked 'do you think that that might have also cost you a few things when you had to wait with making decisions?' — the right idea — got a flat 'No', and folded: 'Yeah, that's fine. I would say, yeah, go think about it. I'm not going to put any pressure on you.'

Correctly not run. The prospect volunteered that the price was fair and benchmarked it himself — 'It's a 1K month average price... I think that it's okay. It's a good price' — and then explicitly ruled money out twice when tested. Running an open wallet here would have manufactured an objection that did not exist.

The real objection has no play: a prospect who processes decisions alone overnight as a matter of temperament rather than because of an unresolved doubt. 'I can't decide something without any analyzing... I have to sleep with this conversation.' He also asked for the offer in writing to support that process and was told nothing written exists. The playbook has no path for a deliberate decider and no document to hand them, which converts a 9/10 buyer into a 24-hour risk.

notes: Phase 3 was well run and the prospect delivered the emotional close himself. Two failures. Phase 5 collapsed against a self-reliant prospect for the second time in three days and the rep had no reframe — against someone who says 'I will keep trying', decline is the wrong lever and opportunity cost is the right one. And the OA play was started well then abandoned at the first flat 'No'. The single highest-leverage fix here is not a rep behaviour at all: he asked for something to read before deciding and there was nothing to send.
